solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skin needs to be treated during second half of weak game

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come during, i.e. in the middle of, the picked pair
the back two letters of the four-letter word weak are taken
something treated is worked on and changed, so the letters of needs are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dermatology note: some skin condition needs treatment during a spell of weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be treated' is the anagram signal for 'needs', giving NDSEE; 'during' puts it between the two letters of the second half of 'weak'.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's pastime where one player looks for others who have concealed themselves is a classic example of a game.

clue.text: Reduction in water supply ruined most of aged flowering plant

indicators.note: a reduction trims the word for the water supply, taking off its final letter

parts.note: a hydrant is a street outlet supplying water

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and put back in a new order
most of the word aged means it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A garden in drought: hosepipe restrictions have ruined an old shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduction in' cuts HYDRANT to HYDRAN; 'most of' cuts AGED to AGE, and 'ruined' rearranges it as GEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a shrub grown for its big heads of blooms, so it is an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: Picked up work in noisy yard for couple of suppliers

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted and read from bottom to top
the short word for a work sits in the word for noisy

parts.note: noisy means loud
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone hears about work going on in a noisy yard involving a pair of firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a sound signal, but here it turns LOPOUD (OP 'in' LOUD) upwards to DUOPOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A market controlled by just two sellers is called by this economics term, so it suits a pair of providers.

clue.text: Dad interrupts one exclamation and suppresses another — they're not necessarily believed

indicators.note: dad, with his load, breaks into the first exclamation

parts.note: aha is a cry of discovery

indicators.note: dad's word holds down, i.e. contains, the second exclamation

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father
a cry is another exclamation

explanation.surface: A father keeps butting in on one outburst and stifling another, and nobody quite believes the tales.
explanation.walkthrough: POP 'suppresses' CRY to make POCRYP, which 'interrupts' AHA: A + POCRYP + HA.
explanation.definitionFit: These writings are of doubtful authenticity, stories whose truth is questioned, so they are not necessarily accepted as true.

clue.text: Line in neat ceramics?

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes in the word for neat

parts.note: neat in the sense of skilful means deft

explanation.surface: A tidy range of pottery: neat lines in ceramic ware.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: this is one kind of ceramics, named after a Dutch town.
explanation.definitionFit: This glazed blue-and-white earthenware from the Netherlands is a well-known kind of pottery, hence an example of the ceramics.

clue.text: Understood island in Middle East picked up self-confidence

indicators.note: the two words go in the turned abbreviation
in a down entry, picked up turns the abbreviation upwards

parts.note: got it means understood it

explanation.surface: Someone grasped that an island in the Middle East had boosted their self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns ME into EM, and GOT + IS go 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An excessive sense of one's own importance is a loose synonym for self-assurance, the clue's setter stretching it to self-belief.

clue.text: A couple of thousand to secure one outsized booth

indicators.note: the pair of thousands secure, i.e. enclose, the other letters

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, so two of them are KK
I is the Roman numeral for one
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Paying a couple of grand to get one oversized stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A small open-fronted stand selling newspapers or snacks is a kind of booth.

clue.text: Against one male withdrawing from protest film

parts.note: V for versus means against
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the male's letter pulls out of the word for a protest

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: One man against the cause quits a protest film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing from' takes M out of DEMO, leaving DEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A recording of moving pictures is a synonym for a film, as with a music promo.

clue.text: Dodgy clergyman — endless weakness for a bar, getting drunk daily, ultimately

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order
ultimately points to the final letter of daily

explanation.surface: A shady churchman, failing in his weakness, heads for the pub to get drunk every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts VICE to VIC; 'getting drunk' turns FOR A BAR into AROFBRA. The Vicar of Bray, from an English song, changed his beliefs to keep his job under each new monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's priest switched his religious loyalties with every new ruler, so he is the byword for an unprincipled cleric.

clue.text: Paint and fuel company to look threatening

parts.note: oil is a fuel
lour means to frown or look menacing

explanation.surface: A paint firm and a fuel company squaring up to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment mixed with linseed is a kind of artist's paint, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Returning fake royal attire

definitions.note: an adjective here, as in returning fire: hitting back

indicators.note: fake letters are counterfeit, made up anew from the original ones

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a counterfeit set of royal robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition, in the sense of returning fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting back in kind, as in returning a blow, is what a vengeful act of reprisal does.

clue.text: Lots of noise? One not commenting regarding team I support

parts.note: a clam is someone who keeps tight-lipped and says nothing
a fan talks of the team they follow as our team

explanation.surface: A fan grumbles about the racket, and a silent onlooker refuses to comment on the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One not commenting' suggests silence, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar of shouting voices is a loud din, the many-voiced racket the definition describes.

clue.text: Material for writer found in indulgence not a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: the writing material is found in the shortened word
not a means the letter a is dropped from the word

parts.note: a treat is an indulgence
ink is what a writer uses

explanation.surface: A writer finds ink in an indulgence that's no jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' takes A out of TREAT, leaving TRET, and INK is 'found in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cheap ornament or bauble worn as an adornment is a modest kind of jewellery.

clue.text: Sport finally sliding into red

indicators.note: the last letter goes into the word for red

parts.note: ruby is a deep red

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of sliding

explanation.surface: A player sliding into a red-carded tackle at the end of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The oval-ball game played with fifteen or thirteen a side is a team sport.

clue.text: Scottish Queen returns in dressy plaid, covering solid figure?

definitions.note: adjectival here: shaped like the solid figure called a pyramid

indicators.note: the jumbled letters cover, i.e. wrap round, the turned name
dressy suggests the plaid is dressed up, its letters rearranged
returns means the queen's name is read backwards

parts.note: Mary, Queen of Scots

explanation.surface: Mary Queen of Scots comes back in a smart tartan, covering her solid figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' gives YRAM, which PIDAL (PLAID rearranged by 'dressy') is 'covering'. The question mark warns that the definition describes the shape rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes something with the form of a pyramid, a geometric solid with triangular sides.

clue.text: Give more food to man lacking a little energy, producing a beam

definitions.note: a phrase for an adjective: giving out light

indicators.note: the abbreviation is missing from the first word

parts.note: to refuel is to top up with fuel, food for an engine
E is the abbreviation for energy
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Serving seconds to a weary man makes him smile broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes the E out of REFUEL, leaving REFUL. 'beam' looks like a smile but is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means shining brightly or radiant, giving out light as a beam does.

clue.text: Verdict: is engaged in air support, getting elevated

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means the letters are read upwards
is is engaged, i.e. held, in the first word

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
aid is support

explanation.surface: A verdict on an airlift: it's caught up in air support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like aviation but means a tune. 'engaged in' puts 'is' after the first letter of the tune, and 'getting elevated' reads the lot upwards, as a down entry allows.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's finding on what illness a patient has is a medical judgement, a verdict on the case.

clue.text: Note workers providing display facility

parts.note: to flag is to note or mark something for attention
staff are workers

explanation.surface: A memo on the workforce supplying a showroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole for flying a banner is equipment for displaying the colours, so it is a facility for display.

clue.text: Keeps suggesting retaining headgear

parts.note: a proofreader's stet marks text to be kept, so stets means keeps
on as in keeping something on, carrying it on rather than dropping it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps hinting that they want to keep their hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: STETS ON reads as keeps on, stet being the editor's mark meaning let it stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat is a kind of headwear.

clue.text: Secretary, mostly disinclined to work inside, finding outdoor area

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the secretary's abbreviation

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: lazy means disinclined to work

explanation.surface: A secretary who mostly can't be bothered to work indoors takes off to the square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter, and 'to work inside' places what is left within the secretary's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An open public square in a town is a synonym for an outdoor space, often paved.

clue.text: European bearing bill is welcomed by drinkers

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: drinkers welcome what is fit to drink

indicators.note: the European bears, i.e. carries inside, the bill

parts.note: a Pole is a European
a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: A European carrying the bar tab is greeted warmly by the drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to drink, like clean water, is safe to consume, which drinkers appreciate.

clue.text: They crash into the beach cars

definitions.meaning: big waves that roll in and break on the shore

explanation.surface: Cars crashing into the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Long breaking waves are called this, and so, informally, are Rolls-Royce cars, hence both senses.

clue.text: Notably Rice pens this

indicators.note: the two words pen, i.e. enclose, the answer's letters

explanation.surface: Tim Rice, notably, writes the words of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Rice is the British lyricist of Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice writes the words for musicals, so what he pens is the words of a song.

clue.text: Location of activity curtailed, restricted by South American destroyer

indicators.note: the shortened word is hemmed in by the two letters
curtailed means docked of its last letter

parts.note: a hive of activity is a busy place

explanation.surface: A busy spot cut short by a South American warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts HIVE to HIV. 'destroyer' looks like a warship but is the Hindu god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief this god is the destroyer within the trinity with Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver.

clue.text: Informed of colour used in sign

indicators.note: the colour word is used, i.e. put, in the sign

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a tint is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone told about the colour used on a signboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told a secret, let in on it, is to be informed of it; the phrase is an idiom.

clue.text: Hike — sorry, rambling — in moorland area?

indicators.note: rambling wanders all over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A walker apologises for a hike wandering off course across the moors.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is an example: this English county is known for moors such as the North York Moors.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern English county contains the North York Moors and much other moorland, so it is one such region.

clue.text: TV programme from outdoors possibly reflected blue as a green shade?

indicators.note: reflected means the letters are seen as in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast
the sky is blue; sky blue is a shade

explanation.surface: A TV show filmed outdoors, with a blue sky reflected as a shade of green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' looks like a colour, but it means the shade of trees, and 'green' the greenwood.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means wooded or covered with bushes, so it describes leafy shade cast by trees.

clue.text: Swindle, not exactly subtle, regarding certain credit cards

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: describing cards paid with by a tap

parts.note: a con is a swindle
tactless means lacking delicacy, hardly subtle

explanation.surface: A scam involving some credit cards that is hardly subtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment cards that work by tapping a reader, with no insertion or touch needed, are known by this term.
